name: Thunder Bluff
summary: Across the plains of Mulgore, Thunder Bluff shelters the tauren above the grasslands. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof founded the city after uniting the nomadic tribes with the New Horde. Rope bridges and wooden lifts link its mesas, while its heights offer safety from centaur marauders and shelter travelers crossing Kalimdor.

sections.title: A Permanent Haven
sections.body: For generations, the tauren wandered across Kalimdor, struggling to survive centaur attacks. During the Third War, Cairne Bloodhoof joined Warchief Thrall, and together the orcs and tauren drove back the centaur and secured Mulgore’s pastures. Cairne led the allied tribes to these natural stone heights to guard their future. Thunder Bluff became their first unified, permanent home in centuries.

sections.title: A City in the Clouds
sections.body: Thunder Bluff stretches across high mesas, joined by rope bridges. The central bluffs hold the markets, bank, inn, and Wind Rider roost. Three more mesas rise beyond them. Hunter Rise serves scouts and trackers. Elder Rise is home to lorekeepers and the Cenarion Circle, led by Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem. Spirit Rise is devoted to spiritual communion, with shelter for shamans and priests and the underground Pools of Vision.

sections.title: Uneasy Unity
sections.body: Cairne Bloodhoof commands the respect of almost every tribe, but the recently settled tauren do not all agree. The Grimtotem tribe, led by Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem, keeps to Elder Rise. Magatha questions Cairne’s conciliatory ways and his allegiance to the Horde’s foreign races. Peace holds under Cairne’s watch, though divisions persist among the council fires above the plains.

faq.answer: High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof rules Thunder Bluff and leads the united tauren tribes. His wisdom, patience, and strength are revered. He founded the city after allying with Thrall’s Horde and driving the centaur from Mulgore.

faq.q: How do you get up to Thunder Bluff?
faq.answer: If you arrive on foot or by kodo, ride one of the large wooden platform lifts on the southwestern or northeastern side of the central mesa. You can also take a Wind Rider flight across Kalimdor.

faq.q: Why did the tauren build on high mesas instead of the ground?
faq.answer: Centaur clans harried the tauren during centuries of nomadic life. The bluffs’ steep cliffs guard their homes, smiths, and sacred elders from attacks on the ground, giving the tauren a place to settle in peace.

faq.q: What are the different rises of the city?
faq.answer: The central mesa has lower, middle, and high tiers, with three outer mesas around it. Hunter Rise holds warriors, hunters, and tracking lodges. Druids, wisemen, and the Grimtotem tribe dwell on Elder Rise. Spirit Rise has shrines to the Earth Mother, trainers of shamans, priests, and mages, and the Pools of Vision below.

faq.q: What are the Pools of Vision?
faq.answer: The Pools of Vision are sacred caverns beneath Spirit Rise. Tauren seers, spiritwalkers, and practitioners of the arcane gather at these quiet, mist-shrouded waters to commune with the elements and read omens about their people’s future.

Magatha Grimtotem is the matriarch and Elder Crone of the Grimtotem clan. She lives on Elder Rise and takes part in Cairne’s council, but distrusts outsiders and challenges the Bloodhoof tribe’s welcoming stance toward the Horde.

angles.text: Thunder Bluff marks your people’s hard-won unity and rebirth after generations of wandering and centaur attacks under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof.
On Elder Rise, Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem leads the Horde’s foremost sanctuary of nature magic. He is the first tauren druid taught in thousands of years.
On Spirit Rise, the Pools of Vision offer a quiet place to honor and hear elemental spirits and the spirits of your tauren ancestors.
Thunder Bluff brings a pastoral presence to the New Horde’s southern reach in Kalimdor, far calmer than Orgrimmar’s harsh battlements.
